metaDescription: Seven cordless and corded hedge trimmers under $100 compared on blade length, cut capacity, battery and weight, with what this budget realistically buys.
expertTake: The WORX WG261 is our top pick under $100 because a 22 inch dual action blade at 5.5 lb on a shared 20V battery handles medium hedges without wearing out your arms. The BLACK+DECKER 18 inch is the value pick for small borders. Skip this price band if you have a long, thick or woody hedge, because a 20V cordless trimmer at this price cuts stems up to about three quarters of an inch and slows in anything thicker.
introParagraphs: A hedge trimmer under $100 is a sensible tool for a small to medium garden: a reciprocating blade, a handle and a battery or a cord. At this price you can choose a 20V cordless model, a corded unit or even a bare tool if you already own the battery. What the budget caps is cut capacity and runtime.

So the questions are blade length, cutting thickness and whether the power source fits your yard. A longer blade covers more per pass but weighs more. Listing prices move, so the $100 cap reflects Amazon prices when this guide was updated. We evaluated these trimmers from spec sheets, listing details and owner feedback patterns, and none of it replaces the maker's safety instructions.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Under $100 you get an 18 to 22 inch dual action blade, a 20V battery or a cord and a cut capacity near 5/8 to 3/4 inch. You do not get a brushless motor, a long reach pole or the power to chew thick woody stems. The WORX WG261 and the BLACK+DECKER 22 inch both list 3/4 inch capacity. Expect to prune thick branches with loppers, not the trimmer.

A 22 inch blade covers more hedge per pass than an 18 inch one but weighs more and tires your arms. The WORX WG261 weighs 5.5 lb in a 22 inch size. The BLACK+DECKER 18 inch is lighter and suits low shrubs. Choose by hedge height and how long you work, since a heavy trimmer overhead is tiring.

The BLACK+DECKER 18 inch lists 5/8 inch capacity while the 22 inch models list 3/4 inch. Capacity is the thickest stem the blades cut cleanly. A dual action blade, in which both blades move, cuts smoother and vibrates less than single action. Steel type matters too, as the TaskStar and DGQHME list SK5 steel, which holds an edge better than basic steel.

The DGQHME lists two batteries and up to 60 minutes, the TaskStar lists 2 x 4.0 Ah and the BLACK+DECKER 22 inch corded runs on 4.0 amps. The CRAFTSMAN is a bare tool, so it only makes sense if you own V20 batteries. A cord never runs out but limits your reach. Pick the power source that matches your hedge and your tool collection.

A wraparound handle, as on the CRAFTSMAN and the corded BLACK+DECKER, lets you switch between vertical and horizontal cuts. A two hand switch or a pressure switch keeps hands away from the blade. Wear eye protection and gloves, and never trim in the rain. A corded unit needs a rated outdoor extension cord.

Do not give up a comfortable weight or a blade guard to save a small amount. It is fine to give up a long pole, a brushless motor and a fancy case. Buy a spare battery or a longer cord before a bigger blade.

faq.q: Is a hedge trimmer under $100 enough?
faq.a: For small to medium hedges, yes. You give up brushless power, a long pole and the strength to cut thick woody stems. Use loppers for branches over about three quarters of an inch.

faq.q: Cordless or corded for a budget trimmer?
faq.a: Corded gives unlimited runtime and costs less. Cordless is freer but limited by battery. Choose by your hedge location.

faq.q: What blade length should I choose?
faq.a: An 18 inch blade suits low shrubs and borders. A 20 to 22 inch blade covers more per pass on taller hedges but weighs more.

faq.q: What does a bare tool mean?
faq.a: It means no battery or charger. The CRAFTSMAN V20 bare tool only makes sense if you already own V20 batteries.

faq.q: How do I keep the blades sharp?
faq.a: Wipe off sap after each use and apply a light oil. Replace or sharpen blades when the cut becomes ragged.
